newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's Alfonsin attacks Peronist policies.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Alfonsin attacks Peronist policies.

text.p: Former Argentine President Raul Alfonsin celebrated on Wednesday his victory 13 years ago at the voting booths by launching a bitter attack on the present "neo-conservative" policies.

Alfonsin's speech, delivered to hundreds of his Radical Party supporters at a stadium rally, marked the 13th anniversary of the return of democracy to Argentina after seven years of brutal dictatorship.
It is also seen as the beginning of his campaign for the presidency in the 1999 elections, although he faces an internal party contest for the candidacy.
"Let us see if we can continue being a country or if we will be turned into a colony," shouted Alfonsin.

In his speech, Alfonsin, who ruled from 1983 to 1989, blamed the world's financial centres and the International Monetary Fund for the "neo-conservative" policies responsible for the current "disaster."

"This is how they have left our country: unemployment is above 20 percent and there is no worse humiliation than wanting to work and not being able to and not being able to bring bread back to the home," he said.
Alfonsin also took a swipe at the country's institutions, saying "sure we have liberty but there is no justice and no transparency (in government)."
Alfonsin was voted in by 52 percent of the vote in 1983.

President Carlos Menem's Peronist Party government, which took over in 1989 after Alfonsin, was re-elected last year after Menem secured a change in the constitution allowing presidential candidates to rule for two terms.
Menem cannot stand again in the 1999 elections but somebody else from the Peronist Party is able to do so.
